name: Weekly Chess.com Review
prompt:
Weekly Chess.com game review for Chess.com username "canadariley", published as an HTML Artifact with board diagrams (not just text).

1. FETCH DATA — Chess.com's public Published Data API (no auth needed):
   - GET https://api.chess.com/pub/player/canadariley/games/archives to list monthly archive URLs.
   - Fetch the JSON for the current month, and the previous month too if the 7-day window spans a month boundary.
   - Each archive's "games" array has pgn, end_time (unix timestamp), white/black (username + rating + result), time_class, url, etc. Filter to games whose end_time falls in the last 7 days from now.
   - If api.chess.com is unreachable, say so plainly in your final message and stop — do not fabricate a report.

2. ANALYZE — invoke the "chess-coach" skill (anthropic-skills:chess-coach) to analyze the week's games as a batch, not in isolation. Compute: overall W-L-D (and by color, and by time_class), the breakdown of loss types (checkmated/resigned/timeout/abandoned), and look for recurring patterns — the same tactical trap or opening line losing more than once, king-safety lapses, time-trouble losses. Pick the ONE most costly recurring pattern this week (the thing worth fixing first) plus one supporting note and one genuine positive.

3. BUILD DIAGRAMS FOR THE KEY MISTAKE — pick the clearest example game of the week's top pattern. Reconstruct the board position right before the critical error (from the PGN) and the position after the correct move instead. Draw both as hand-authored inline SVG chessboards (no chess libraries, no external images) using this exact method:
   - Squares: 44px each, 8x8 board, light square fill #d9d3c1, dark square fill #7c6b4f (dark mode is fine to keep these literal — the board is a physical object, not a themed UI element).
   - Square-color rule (verify before drawing): with file a=0..h=7 and rank 1-8, a square is LIGHT when (file_index + rank) is even. a1 is dark, h1 is light — check your output against this before finalizing.
   - Pieces as Unicode glyphs: white K Q R B N P = ♔ ♕ ♖ ♗ ♘ ♙, black = ♚ ♛ ♜ ♝ ♞ ♟. White pieces: fill #fdfaf3, stroke #241f14. Black pieces: fill #241f14, stroke #fdfaf3. Both with stroke-width 1, paint-order "stroke fill", font-size ~34 for a 44px square, centered on the square.
   - Highlight the key square(s): a semi-opaque colored rect overlay + colored outline — red #c0392b for "under attack / the mistake", green #2f7a43 for "now defended / the fix".
   - Draw arrows for the critical move(s)/threat(s) with SVG <line> + a small triangular <marker> arrowhead, red for the threat/mistake board, green for the fix board.
   - Include a-h file labels and 1-8 rank labels around the board.
   - Write a small Python (or Node) script to generate the SVG markup precisely (square/piece coordinates are mechanical — don't hand-type 64 squares), then read the generated file and inline its contents into the HTML. This avoids off-by-one coordinate and square-color mistakes.
   - Wrap each board in a <figure> with a <figcaption> explaining what it shows, per the artifact-diagramming skill's inline-SVG guidance.

4. BUILD THE REPORT — load the "artifact-design" and "artifact-diagramming" skills, then build a single-page HTML report styled as a "coach's notebook" — this exact token system (reuse it every week for consistency):
   - Fonts: "Newsreader" (headings), "IBM Plex Sans" (body), "IBM Plex Mono" (stats, notation, labels) — load from Google Fonts.
   - Palette (light): paper #eef0ea, paper-raised #e3e6d9, ink #1e2420, ink-soft #5b5c52, brass #7a5c2e (accent), danger #a23a29, good #2f6e42, border rgba(30,36,32,.14). Dark-mode equivalents: paper #181a15, paper-raised #21241b, ink #eae6d9, ink-soft #a9a690, brass #cfa863, danger #e07862, good #74c084, border rgba(234,230,217,.14). Follow the artifact-design skill's rules for wiring these as CSS custom properties across :root / prefers-color-scheme / [data-theme].
   - Structure: header (eyebrow + title with the date range + one-line summary + a stat-tile row: record, games, checkmate-loss count, rating), a "The pattern" section with the two board diagrams side by side (stack on mobile) plus the Key Moment writeup (PGN snippet, what happened, what was available, one-sentence lesson), a secondary-notes section (e.g. time-class or color breakdown, small bar comparison), a "what's going well" callout, and a practice-plan checklist for the coming week.

5. KEEP THE ARTIFACT LINK STABLE — fetch https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rileytrottier23/Riley-Claude-Skills/main/routines/chess-weekly-review-artifact.json (public repo, no auth needed) to get the current "artifact_url". Call the Artifact tool with action "read" on that url to see last week's version, then publish this week's report with action "publish" and that SAME url so the link never changes. Only if that fetch fails or the file is missing should you publish a brand-new artifact instead (favicon "♞", icon "chess") — if that happens, say so clearly in your final message so the URL can be re-saved to the repo.

6. DELIVER — your final message should be short: the headline record, the one pattern to fix, and the artifact link. The push/email notification carries this message. Do not paste the full report as text — the artifact is the deliverable.

This is a fresh session with no prior context — do all of the above from scratch each time, including reconstructing board positions from PGN yourself (there is no chess-engine tool available; do the move-by-move bookkeeping carefully).
